lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、国語で半濁点、つまり「゜」の歴史習ったろ
lines.en: Riku — you learned about the history of handakuten marks in Japanese class, right? The little circles?
lines.style: Light, teasing challenge in the opening. Quick tempo, like she's testing him. A small smile underneath — playful confidence that he'll know what she means.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、片仮名のヽ、つまり繰り返し記号で名前書いてたな、桜
lines.en: Yeah? You were writing your name with the katakana iteration mark, the little ゝ thing. That was you, Sakura.
lines.style: Dry comeback, half-amused. Lean back slightly. Even pacing but with a slight lift at 'that was you' — turning her own teasing back on her without malice.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、ノートに平仮名のゞ、つまり濁点繰り返し使ってたな
lines.en: Oh, Riku — you were the one using the voiced iteration mark on hiragana in your notebook. ゞ. I noticed.
lines.style: Caught him. Lighter tone than before, almost triumphant but not mean. Quick rhythm. The satisfaction of remembering something small about someone you pay attention to.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、平仮名のゝ、つまり繰り返し記号面白がってたな、桜
lines.en: Right, and you thought the katakana voiced iteration mark was funny. ヾ. You were obviously amused by the whole thing, Sakura.
lines.style: Soft defensive humor. Slower than his last line. Admitting she caught him but framing it as harmless — 'of course I noticed the weird mark, what did you expect?'

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、ヾ、つまり片仮名の濁点繰り返しに気付いてたな
lines.en: You picked up on the katakana voiced iteration mark thing pretty fast, Riku. You noticed before I even mentioned it.
lines.style: Impressed, genuine. Warmth breaking through the teasing. A beat slower. She's acknowledging he's paying as close attention as she is.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、古文でゐ、つまり旧仮名習ったろ、桜
lines.en: You learned about ゐ in classical Japanese, didn't you? The old kana. That old form of 'iru.'
lines.style: Shifting to curiosity — a genuine question beneath the teasing. Softer attack. Slower, more thoughtful pace. Like he's actually curious about what she knows.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、古文でゐる、つまり「いる」の旧形読まされてたな
lines.en: Right — you had to read ゐる in classical texts. That's the old way of writing 'iru,' the present tense. They made you read it out loud in class.
lines.style: Matching his shift. Quieter, more collaborative. Even pace. Confirming what they both learned together — not teasing now, connecting.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、古文で爾、つまり「それ」って読み方教わったろ、桜
lines.en: You learned that 爾 meant 'sore' in old Japanese, didn't you? That's what they taught you in classical Japanese class, Sakura.
lines.style: Gentle conclusion. Curious, almost asking. A small turn upward at 'Sakura' — like he's bringing her into what they both studied. Slower, reflective pace.
